Golden rule, motherfucker.|Lucy to [[the Ghoul]]|sound=Lucy golden rule MF.ogg}} '''Lucy MacLean''' is the main protagonist of the [[Fallout (TV series)|''Fallout'' TV series]] and one of the show's central characters alongside [[The Ghoul]] and [[Maximus]]. The daughter of [[Hank MacLean|Hank]] and [[Rose MacLean]] and the sister of [[Norm MacLean]], Lucy is a lifelong dweller of [[Vault 33]] of the [[Three Vaults]] based in what was once [[Boneyard|Los Angeles]]. In [[Timeline (2250-2300)#2296|2296]], she embarks on a mission into the [[wasteland]] to save her father after he is kidnapped during a raider attack led by a mysterious woman named [[Lee Moldaver|Moldaver]]. ==Background== Lucy was born to Hank and Rose MacLean within Vault 33 sometime in the mid 2270s, followed later by her younger brother Norman. Sometime during Lucy's adolescence, her mother Rose became suspicious of the Vaults' doctrine about the surface being inhospitable and after her concerns were dismissed by her husband, she took her children and fled from Vault 33, angering Hank because he viewed this as endangering their children, both in terms of a physical risk[[Hank MacLean]]: ''"Lucy? I loved your mother. But she stopped being your mother when she left home. When she took you into danger. You've seen what it's like up here. Everyone equally afraid, equally miserable. Forced to do horrible things in order to survive. Lucy... I had to make a choice. Between their violent world and our peaceful one. And I believe, Lucy, I know I made the right choice."''
({{FOTV|1|8}}) but also an ideological one, as he feared they would be influenced by the violence and survival instincts instilled by life in the wasteland, which would ruin Vault-Tec's mission for their Vault.[[Hank MacLean]]: ''"We never got to discuss All Quiet, did we? I guess we were waiting 'til after the wedding. Right? That end, that was a humdinger, huh?"''
Lucy MacLean: ''"I didn't finish it."''
Hank: ''"That's okay. You've been busy. What did you think about the parts that you did read?"''
Lucy: ''"I found it very upsetting."''
Hank: ''"Can't disagree with you there. What aspect upset you most?"''
Lucy: ''"[scoffs]"''
Hank: ''"To me, the most troubling was that everyone seemed to be fighting over nothing. The French and the German, what was the difference between them, really? I mean, other than the uniforms? I saw the same thing up on the surface. People fighting over the most petty things, like bottle caps. Is that what you saw when you were there? But, you know, some things just never change. People just wanna kill each other, don't they? I think it's the only way for people to feel safe. It's ironic. To feel safe, we have to hurt people. Even kill them, because the-- [...] It's crazy... the war instinct, hm?"''
Lucy: ''"I'm bringing you back to Vault 33 to face justice. For murdering the citizens of Shady Sands. You have the right to remain silent until the Vault Council assigns you a legal counselor."''
Hank: ''"For a second there, I thought the Wasteland had changed you."''
[...]
Lucy: ''"What are you doing?"''
Hank: ''"Surrendering."''
Hank: ''"I did what I did to protect you. But maybe it came at too high a price. And there comes a time in a man's life when he has to take responsibility for what he's done, and for me, that time has come. You have come, Sugarbomb."''
({{FOTV|2|6}}) Sometime after leaving the Vault, the MacLeans reached [[Shady Sands]], the capital city of the [[New California Republic]], where Rose met and formed a close relationship with [[Lee Moldaver]]. However, neither Lucy nor Norm can recall much of this time, seemingly being too young at the time to form complete memories. Despite this, Lucy would vaguely remember her mother taking her to play in a field under the sun, feeling its warmth, but eventually concluded that this was instead the light over Vault 33's crop field.[[Lucy MacLean]]: ''"Up until I was six, I really thought that the big light on our farm was the sun. My mom used to take me to play out under that light, and I swear I could feel the sun baking my skin... After my mom was gone, I realized it was just her that made it all feel so real."''
({{FOTV|1|5}}) At some point after coming to Shady Sands, Rose was found there by Hank, but she refused to come back with him. Instead, Hank took his children back from Rose, returning with them to Vault 33, where he convinced Lucy and Norm that their mother died as a victim of the "Plague of '77."{{cn}} Sometime later in 2283, Hank arranged for a [[Nuclear weapons|nuclear device]] to be delivered into the streets of Shady Sands and remotely detonated it to wipe out the post-War nation, then shortly after, going to read his daughter a story at her request.{{FOTV|2|2}} [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 051.png|thumb|left|200px|Lucy and [[Steph Harper]] doing work for the Pipefitters Association]] Growing up in Vault 33, Lucy lived a relatively happy, carefree and privileged lifestyle. However, she contributed to the maintenance and wellbeing of her Vault and community whenever she could. Among her known achievements were memberships in the Young Pipefitter's Association (shared with her best friend [[Steph Harper]], a [[Vault 31]] transplant); gymnastics club; Fencing Team C; intermediate Phys. Ed.; and riflery.{{FOTV|1|1}} She also gained some basic knowledge about the workings of [[power armor]]. According to Lucy herself, her primary passion was teaching American history to the Vault's children, with a focus on ethics. Private time with her family was spent watching movies or gardening with her father, or engaging in family book club discussions with her father and Norm. Lucy was raised with little to no knowledge about the outside world except for what she had seen in books (like ''[[War and Peace]]'' and ''[[All Quiet on the Western Front]]'') and films or been taught by her father. Outside of her immediate family, Lucy interacted closely with her first cousin [[Chet (TV series)|Chet]], with whom she did "10 years of cousin stuff" in a non-detailed manner; while this casual intimate relationship between cousins is permitted in the community for children, cousin marriage is not. ==''Fallout'' TV series== ===Season 1=== {{Quotation|A resident of Vault 33, Lucy actively contributes to the well-being of her community. She participates in the Young Pipefitter’s Association, gymnastics club, fencing team 3, intermediate Phys. Ed., and riflery. Her primary passion is teaching American history with a focus on ethics. In her personal time she watches movies with her dad, gardens (also with her dad), and enjoys family book club (again, with her dad — Norm chooses not to participate). She’s upbeat and uncannily direct with an all-American can-do spirit.|[[Fallout season 1 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 1 character description]]}} ====[[The End (episode)|The End]]==== [[File:FOTV wedding.png|thumb|250px|Lucy being married to Monty]] As the show begins, Lucy gives her marriage application to the Vault 33 governing council ([[Woody Thomas]], [[Betty Pearson]], and [[Reg McPhee]]), which they quickly accept. She has an arranged marriage with [[Monty (TV series)|Monty]], a resident of [[Vault 32]]. After they consummate, Lucy hears screams outside her room. Alarmed, she scans Monty with her Pip-Boy and realizes he is irradiated and must be a raider from the surface. Lucy survives his attack, eventually stabbing him in the neck, leaving him unconscious. She heals herself with a [[stimpak]] and arms herself with a tranquilizer gun during the raider attack. During the fight in the atrium, Lucy hides Norm in a floor storage space and watches her father drown Monty to death in the apple-bobbing tub. [[Lee Moldaver]], posing as the overseer of Vault 32, abducts Hank. [[File:Lucy first time outside Vault 33.webp|thumb|left|250px|Lucy leaving Vault 33]] Lucy proposes organizing a search party to rescue her father during an emergency council meeting. The Vault council disapprove of opening the Vault door, as they don't want to give up their new authority. Rather than stay put, Lucy takes the opportunity to leave when the others are not around. She enlists help from Norm, who acts as a lookout, and Chet, who unlocks the elevator to the Vault door and helps unseal the exterior door from the inside. Chet insists on coming with Lucy since the outside world is dangerous, but she tranquilizes him. She hugs Norm goodbye and leaves the Vault, ignoring Reg and [[Davey (TV series)|Davey]]'s shouts for her to stop. ====[[The Target]]==== [[File:FOTV S1 Amazon promo 9.jpg|thumb|250px|Lucy with Wilzig and Ma June in Filly]] After a day traveling through the Wasteland, Lucy stops to rest for the night. While sleeping by a campfire, Lucy encounters [[Siggi Wilzig]], an Enclave defector transporting a valuable artifact to Moldaver for a [[cold fusion]] project. He tries to warn her about the dangers of the wasteland and urges her to go home before disappearing into the night. The next day, Lucy makes it to the settlement of [[Filly]], where she is laughed at and looked down on by [[Ma June]], a storekeeper who views Vault dwellers as naive. As Wilzig arrives in town and has another exchange with Lucy, they are then confronted by [[the Ghoul]], who is tracking Wilzig for a bounty. A shootout ensues as the Ghoul shoots Wilzig's left foot off, then kills several gunfighters who try to take him down. After Wilzig's dog [[CX404]] is stabbed trying to defend her master, Lucy unsuccessfully tries to deescalate the situation peacefully. When the Ghoul takes a step towards her, she shoots him with a tranquilizer dart, which proves ineffective, though [[Maximus]] soon arrives in power armor, tackles Lucy out of the way as the Ghoul shoots at her, and keeps him at bay while Lucy and Ma June try to save Wilzig. When the situation with The Ghoul is resolved, Ma June reveals to Lucy that Moldaver is her client. Lucy attempts to take an injured Wilzig across the wasteland, but he succumbs to his leg injury and takes a cyanide pill. At his request, once he dies, Lucy decapitates him with a chainsaw and takes his head. ====[[The Head]]==== [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 035.png|thumb|250px|left|Lucy held at gunpoint by the Ghoul]] Lucy travels with Wilzig's head and stops along the flooded [[Hollywood Boulevard]]. She briefly feeds a fawn, but it is devoured by a [[Gulper (TV series)|gulper]]. The gulper attacks Lucy, but she manages to free herself by using her tranq gun. The gulper swallows the head and swims away. Before she can pursue him, the Ghoul (who has been using CX404 to track Wilzig's scent) catches up to her and captures her. He ties Lucy to a waterside pulley and repeatedly dunks her in the water as bait to draw out the gulper. They successfully do so, but the gulper attacks too quickly for them to handle, and Lucy accidentally destroys the Ghoul's [[inhaler vial]]s when she uses his saddle bag to stop the gulper from swallowing her. Angered by her actions, the Ghoul takes Lucy prisoner and drags her away due to her needing to find new vials, reasoning that they will be able to return before the gulper fully digests the head. ====[[The Ghouls]]==== [[File:FOTV The gory finger scene.png|thumb|250px|Lucy getting her finger sliced off]] On their journey, Lucy and the Ghoul encounter a friend of the latter's, [[Roger (TV series)|Roger]], a fellow ghoul who is on the verge of turning feral. Realizing that his friend is beyond the point of saving, the Ghoul gets him to reminisce about happier times before shooting him dead. As Lucy gets on his case about his cruelty, she reveals that her last name is 'MacLean', causing the Ghoul to realize that she's the daughter of [[Barb Howard|his wife's]] pre-War assistant. He also forces her to carve up Roger's body for meat. Sometime later, Lucy drinks some irradiated water out of desperation. While the Ghoul is having a coughing fit, she attempts to flee, but he captures her after she unwisely decides to stand in the same spot. She bites his right index finger off, and he cuts off her right index finger to make things even. The Ghoul soon drags Lucy to the [[Super Duper Mart (TV series)|Super Duper Mart]], where he offers her to [[Snip Snip]] in exchange for two months' worth of vials, assuring the Mister Handy that she is in pristine condition, apart from her missing finger. Snip Snip acts courteously to Lucy, and surgically reattaches a decaying index finger to replace Lucy's missing digit. Lucy tries to beg him for help, saying that she feared the Ghoul was sending her to become a sex slave, to which Snip Snip reacts with shock and disgust; he intends to harvest her organs instead. Before Lucy can do anything, Snip Snip fires a tranquilizer dart at Lucy's chest, knocking her out cold. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 078.png|thumb|250px|left|Lucy trying to avoid Snip Snip's organ-harvesting surgery]] Snip Snip straps Lucy to a gurney and brings her to [[Huey]] and [[Squirrel (TV series)|Squirrel]], informing them of the transaction. They tell him to go through with it. He brings Lucy into the operating room and prepares to use his buzzsaw to cut her open, saying that it will be painless, with only a "snip-snip" to be done. She can escape from the gurney; however, she uses a nearby defibrillator to shock Snip Snip and tries using him as leverage to free herself and the captive ghouls. Huey and Squirrel, however, regarded Snip Snip as nothing more than an oversized air conditioner, but allowed her to go when she threatened them with a makeshift weapon, as well as meeting her demand of freeing the ghouls. They complied, freeing those who hadn't lost their cognitive functions, but this didn't satisfy Lucy, and she threatened to kill the pair with a poisonous cleanser, which she fired at their couch and began to dissolve the material. They then comply and release the others, but Lucy almost immediately regrets this decision, witnessing their feral nature as they charge toward her and the others. She hides from the ferals, who kill Huey and Squirrel before leaving. Afterward, only one ghoul named [[Martha (TV series)|Martha]] remains, but she nearly attacks Lucy, leading her to pick up a [[10mm pistol (Fallout 4)|10mm pistol]] to kill her. Outside, she finds the Ghoul on the ground, needing the vials inside the market. Despite his prior mistreatment of her, she decides that she's not going to let him meet the same fate as the ghouls in the mart, and gives him the vials before walking off, showing how she is learning how to blend her ideals with the demands of reality. ====[[The Past]]==== Following her liberation from the Ghoul and nearly having her organs harvested, Lucy comes across Maximus once more, who was imprisoned in his own armor by his squire [[Thaddeus]], who removed his [[Fusion core (TV series)|fusion core]]. Several [[Radroach (TV series)|radroaches]] crawled upon his armor, leading her to blast them off with her handgun. She can lift his helmet's visor, but suffers from radiation sickness, leading him to offer her his [[RadAway]] if she frees him. With that, she frees him and collapses from her illness. True to his word; however, Maximus treats Lucy's radiation sickness, and both decide to work together to find Thaddeus and regain the head the Gulper had coughed up. [[File:FOTV Official Trailer Still 113.png|thumb|250px|Viewing Shady Sands with Maximus]] While tracking Thaddeus, Lucy chats with Maximus about the state of affairs on the surface, asking what has happened since the Vault dwellers went underground. Reaching a bridge, they come across two [[Cannibalism|cannibals]], [[Javin]] and [[Rink]], who attempt to kill them, but Maximus takes Lucy's gun and kills the pair, though he is shot in the process. Sometime later, they come across the ruins of Shady Sands, which Maximus reveals was once his home before the Brotherhood took him in. Lucy is shocked to hear that civilization has returned to the surface without the Vault dwellers and struggles to reconcile this with the stated purpose of Vault 33, which is to come to the surface and rebuild civilization on its own. Soon, Lucy discovers Maximus' wound is more serious than he claims. She takes him looking for medical supplies, eventually coming across [[Hawthorne Medical Laboratories]]. While searching for supplies in the building, they both end up falling through a trap door, waking up inside [[Vault 4]]. ====[[The Trap]]==== After landing in Vault 4, Lucy and Maximus find themselves meeting with [[Birdie]] while the Vault's medical staff [[Nose Edmundson|Dr. Edmundson]] and [[Powell|Nurse Powell]] treat Maximus' wound, extracting a rotten tooth and revealing that was what he was shot with. Birdie explains that they will be kept in quarantine for a while longer to protect the Vault from surface contaminants. While staying there, Maximus tells Lucy she smells nice, which she interprets to be an attempt at flirting, responding by inviting him to have sex with her. Maximus, who did not receive any sexual education in the Brotherhood, tells her that it seems weird. Though Lucy assures him that sexual responses are natural, he refuses, saying the Brotherhood discourages sexual relationships. After leaving quarantine, they meet the overseer [[Benjamin (TV series)|Benjamin]] and learn that the Vault is open to refugees from the destroyed Shady Sands. It's then they learn that all levels of the Vault are open, except for level 12. Maximus feels slightly uncomfortable with the Vault, believing it to be a cult, although Lucy shrugs it off. While there, however, Lucy becomes horrified by the vault's worship of someone called the "Flame Mother," who is revealed to be Lee Moldaver. She then decides to venture to the 12th level of the vault, learning of the vault's genetic experimentation. She is caught, however, and attempts to fight her way out, ultimately getting herself captured and imprisoned. ====[[The Radio]]==== Following her capture, Lucy learns more about what transpired in the vault via [[holotape]] and is then brought before the others to receive punishment. Believing she is about to be executed, it's revealed she is merely expelled from the vault and released with some supplies. Then, Maximus, who had adjusted to life in the vault, swipes their fusion core, powers up his recently retrieved armor, and uses it to free Lucy. Lucy then explains they were letting her go, leaving Maximus to feel embarrassed about the whole thing. They then leave the vault, but not before Lucy convinces Maximus to leave the fusion core with them. Reluctantly, Maximus complies and tosses it down the trap door, where they fell into prior. After returning to the fusion core, Lucy invites Maximus to live with her in her vault after she rescues her father. Maximus then reveals his name isn't Titus, but Maximus, and that Knight Titus was a person he let die for threatening him and took his power armor afterward. Lucy admits that she has done some horrible things during her journey through the wasteland, so she doesn't hold Maximus' past against him. Lucy and Maximus remain together, continuing on their journey. [[File:Lucy Maximus kiss.png|thumb|left|250px|Lucy and Maximus' farewell kiss]] They finally meet up with Thaddeus, who's called for reinforcements and extraction. It's then that he gets defensive when the pair approach him, causing him to trigger a nearby booby trap, leaving Thaddeus with a hole in his neck, but not killed. After Thaddeus is instantaneously healed of his wound, Maximus suspects that Thaddeus may be turning into a [[ghoul]]. Thaddeus becomes in distress as the Brotherhood will surely kill him now. Maximus offers to return to the Brotherhood to prevent them from finding Thaddeus if he gives them Wilzig's head. Thaddeus agrees and thanks Maximus for his help, then leaves. Maximus and Lucy share a kiss before going in separate directions. Maximus creates a fake [[critic|decoy head]] to pass off to the Brotherhood, while Lucy goes to Moldaver with the real head and rescues her father. Lucy tells Maximus to find her in Vault 33 someday. ====[[The Beginning]]==== Separated from Maximus, Lucy makes her way to the Griffith Observatory, Moldaver's base of operations. Arriving in the main operating room, she finds Moldaver waiting for her at a table next to a restrained feral ghoul, with her father caged nearby. She hands over the head and demands the release of her father, to which Moldaver agrees, but not before revealing why she kidnapped him. Moldaver reveals the truth about Vaults 31-33 and that Hank was an executive at Vault-Tec who was cryogenically frozen for two centuries. When Lucy's mother, Rose, found out, she escaped Vault 33 with Lucy and Norm, and they settled in Shady Sands with Moldaver. But when Hank found out, he orchestrated the destruction of Shady Sands, killing thousands of innocent people and taking Lucy and Norm back to Vault 33. Moldaver reveals the head contains a concealed capsule of cold fusion technology, part of research that Moldaver herself was working on, which allows for endless power. Hank was needed because he knew the access code to unlock it. Realizing Hank was responsible for her mother's fate—not death by starvation as she once believed, but the radiation from the bomb on Shady Sands had turned her into the very ghoul sitting at Moldaver's table—Lucy forces Hank to give Moldaver the code. [[File:FOTV Lucy aiming at Hank.png|thumb|250px|Lucy contemplates killing her father]] Once Moldaver gets the code, she attempts to activate her machine, only to realize the Brotherhood of Steel is coming into force. Lucy remains inside the observatory, where Maximus finds her and frees her father. She then reveals to him her father's involvement in destroying Shady Sands. In a rage, Maximus tries to attack Hank, only for Hank to knock him unconscious. Lucy then picks up his gun and aims it at Hank, heartbroken and angered at his actions, but hesitates to pull the trigger. The Ghoul arrives and grazes Hank with a bullet that cuts a gash across his left cheek, demanding to know where his wife and daughter are located. Rather than answer, Hank turns around and flies off. The Ghoul extends an olive branch to Lucy, inviting her to join him in tracking down Hank and, hopefully, his family; if she stays with Maximus, she will likely be killed by the Brotherhood of Steel. Lucy chooses to shoot her mother to end her suffering before following the Ghoul, leaving Maximus with the Brotherhood. Before leaving, Lucy tells an unconscious Maximus that she'll find him again. Lucy and the Ghoul stop at the [[Hollywood Forever]] mausoleum, where they reunite with [[CX404|Dogmeat]] and she arms herself with a rifle before setting off in pursuit of Hank. ===Season 2=== {{Quotation|Lucy is an optimistic Vault Dweller whose all-American, can-do spirit is tested when her father is kidnapped. For the first time in her life, she leaves Vault 33 to pursue her father’s captors across The Wasteland where she encounters violence and creatures she’d never imagined, along with shocking truths about everything she thought she knew about life above and below the irradiated surface.|[[Fallout season 2 Amazon overview|''Fallout'' season 2 character description]]}} ====[[The Innovator]]==== Sometime after entering the [[Mojave Wasteland]], the pair's travel supplies ran out. They made it as far as the town of [[Novac]], which they discovered had been taken over by a gang of [[Great Khans]] led by [[Nick the Prick]]. Lucy advocated for the diplomatic approach of just asking them for their supplies, but the Ghoul's plan won out: Lucy would turn him in to the Khans for their long-standing bounty on him, then once she received the caps reward, she would rescue him from captivity and they would eliminate all of them and acquire their supplies. It is implied that they had also carried out this scam multiple times prior to Novac. However, when it comes time for her to shoot the Ghoul down from his noose, she declines to go through with the plan to kill them and instead reveals herself trying to negotiate. As the Ghoul is left struggling, she attempts to convince the Khans to let them go with their supplies instead of forcing her to resort to violence. Once the Khans rebuke her offer, Lucy switches to the original plan and frees the Ghoul. The pair start a shootout, with Lucy sniping from the [[Dinky the T-Rex]] statue and noticeably trying to only inflict non-fatal wounds on the Khans. The Ghoul, however, goes straight for the lethal option, using various means and weapons to take out the Khans one by one, while Lucy shakes her head in frustration at her companion's brutal tactics. After disposing of all the Great Khans, the two and [[CX404|Dogmeat]] depart from Novac a short time later. Lucy, the Ghoul and Dogmeat walk across a flat desert plain as the two bicker over Lucy's reluctance to kill her enemies ruining the plan to rob the Great Khans and generally being a hindrance in the Ghoul's eyes. They eventually reach a hill overlooking the expanse of New Vegas. Lucy is awestruck by the sight of Vegas, and how the city from a distance looks virtually unchanged from its pre-War glory. The Ghoul reveals that the city's air defenses shot down most of the missiles. However, when Lucy questions why "they" did not do that for the rest of America, the Ghoul sneers that there was no "they," and Vegas only survived because of one man - [[Robert House]]. Lucy assumes that the Ghoul's family headed to Las Vegas because it's safe, but he counters that nowhere around House is safe. On the trail to New Vegas, Lucy and the Ghoul continue arguing about his belief in finding his family with her father until they come across the body of a wastelander who was crushed to death by Hank in his stolen [[T-60 power armor (TV series)|T-60 power armor]]. Further along, they encounter a roadside soup shack run by an elderly woman, [[Old Woman Gretch|Gretch]]. Despite the Ghoul's initial plan to threaten her, Lucy gets him to stand by while she tries diplomacy. She tries to be friendly by buying Gretch's "[[flea soup]]" for 2 caps but quickly regrets the decision once she takes a cautionary sip. Directly asking for information on Hank, Gretch reveals that he did come by and had kidnapped [[Sunburned man|her son]], likely killing him. Lucy tries to express sympathy but is told by Gretch that she only regrets that her son can't pay her the money he owes, and Lucy awkwardly sympathizes for her lost money instead before leaving. Following Gretch's directions, the Ghoul questions Lucy about her goals once they eventually find her father, and sneers at her assertion that she plans to bring him to "justice." They eventually find Hank's heavy footprints taking them to the site of an abandoned [[Starlight Drive-in Theatre (TV series)|Starlight Drive-In Theatre]], in the meantime the Ghoul questioning her rationale for seeking justice in a lawless wasteland and Lucy arguing back that it was what she was raised to believe. As they explore, the Ghoul is momentarily distracted seeing that his old film ''[[A Man and His Dog|A Man and His Dog 3]]'' was listed on the marquee. Lucy and Dogmeat, meanwhile, continue following the footprints up to the screen display, where Lucy sees a destroyed part of it exposing the open blast door entrance to [[Vault 24]]. She tries to adjust her appearance a little before entering. Inside the foyer of the Vault, Lucy is taken aback by the overgrown state of the Vault as compared to the well-maintained state of her home Vault. She questions the Ghoul about his experience finding other Vaults, learning that he always carried a sense of dread every time he found one, fearing that it might be where he would find out the fates of his family, for good, bad, or far worse. Lucy shares her experience about her previous trip to [[Vault 4]],{{FOTV|1|6}} and the experiments that went on there, but the Ghoul counters that Vault 4 was a best-case scenario among the full compilation. She argues that her Vault was less weird from her perspective, but he remarks that she does not know the worst of what goes on in the Vaults. He manually guides her over to use her Pip-Boy for powering on the elevator, then points out Hank's tracks show him both entering and leaving the Vault. The Ghoul then retrieves a hat with a communist insignia from the floor and shows it to Lucy before they enter the elevator and descend into Vault 24. On the lower level, they discover that Vault 24's experiment was centered on testing out a [[brain-computer interface chip]], with the experiments consisting of exposing American test subjects to communist propaganda to brainwash them. Lucy investigates the Vault's computer network but discovers that her father removed the hard drive containing the research data. They then notice a trail of food crumbs leading into a back-end operating room with a box of [[Sugar Bombs]] left on the table—in reference to Hank's nickname for Lucy, "Sugarbomb." A noise alerts them to the presence of Gretch's son, implanted with a chip that Hank uses to deliver a message to Lucy where he tells her to go home and stop chasing him; he ends it by increasing the chip's power until the man's head explodes and splatters them both in gore. Lucy is confronted by her father who begins to talk to her about the brain control chips, saying that while the original creator of the chips Robert House wanted to turn men into robots, he wanted to bring some personality to them by using Welch as the catalyst. Due to her personality matrix being the ideal standard for personnel. Well-meaning, sweet and non-threatening. When Lucy asks what his end-game is, he reveals a miniature version of the chip, remarking that soon no one will be able to tell who has it or does not, with the only sign a small scar on their neck. As the legionary who stranged her earlier arrives, Hank tells her that after she receives it, she will be his little girl again. She calls him insane, which shocks him, before he tells her that she does not mean it, and soon she will not. Lucy attacks the legionary with her crowbar, but he again strangles her. Hank begins to place the chip into Lucy's neck as she struggles, although he stops as the legionary is killed by a throwing knife from the Ghoul. He then shoots Hank in the buttock, telling him that if it was up to him, he would have killed him, but it is Lucy's decision as he slides a pistol to her. She looks down on her father weighing up the decision, as the Ghoul walks away. Lucy leads Hank out onto the New Vegas Strip, having planted the chip into his neck, while holding the pistol and a chip remote. He remarks upon the view, before Lucy tells him that she dreamed of the world outside the Vault. He then tells her that he almost wanted to go back to the Vault, so he could see familiar faces and deducts that they are not going back to the Vault. Lucy remarks that the surface changes a person, although Hank tries to convince her to join him in stopping the Legion. She asks him to tell her what he was really doing in Vegas, although he asks what she will do once he does. She admits that she will turn him into the father she wished she had. He tells her that the surface was the real experiment, not the Vaults, which surprises Lucy. He also reveals that he has already sent people with the new miniature chips out into the wasteland with orders written pre-War. Lucy tries to get him to reveal what he has done, but using his own hidden remote, he turns on his own chip. Lucy tries to stop him, but discovers he is now effectively a shell. She hugs him, before he awakens and seemingly not recognizing her, asks to wipe away a smudge from her face. Through tears she watches the now blank faced Hank, leaving him there. [[File:FTV S2E8 Still 151.png|thumb|250px|Lucy reunites with Maximus]] As she takes in the surroundings, Maximus calls out to her and the two embrace. As Legion troops enter Vegas, Lucy and Maximus reach the penthouse of the Lucky 38, where they see House's computer bank with a "Signal Lost" screen. As the two look over New Vegas, Lucy tells him that there will be a war and it will be her fault. Maximus simply tells her "Welcome to the Wasteland." Unseen by the two, House appears for a split second on his monitor before vanishing again. ==Personality== {{Quotation|I may end up looking like you... but I'll never be like you. Golden Rule, motherfucker.|Lucy to [[The Ghoul]]|sound=golden rule.mp3}} [[File:The End episode banner.jpg|thumb|250px|Lucy looking forward to her future]] Lucy is an active contributor to the well-being of her community, such as doing Vault maintenance using her repair skills, or gardening. She relishes being challenged, as seen with her participation in various physical activities. However, she downplays her skill with guns, claiming her aim is not always the best, even though she is depicted getting bullseyes. She enjoys reading, watching movies and learning about history. She has been described as being kind, charming, plucky, and strong. Whenever an issue arises, Lucy will bravely jump to the occasion to get things done, such as when she tries to resolve the violence in Filly by talking down the Ghoul, or when she investigates the restricted area of Vault 4 by herself against Overseer Benjamin's directions. This trait may have been the result of her father having been overseer. Lucy strongly believes in the "Golden Rule," which is to treat others as she wishes to be treated. However, Lucy still displays the behaviors of someone who has been indoctrinated by Vault-Tec, such as when she bluntly asks Monty about his sperm count and when she abruptly asks Maximus if he'd like to have sex with her while the two of them are quarantined in Vault 4's intake room, blurring the lines of her being a sex positive character versus an indoctrinated one. More evidence of possible programming is her over-the-top bubbly personality; she says "Okie-dokie" in many situations, such as when she approves something, when she does not get what she wants, or even when doing something mentally challenging, such as preparing to posthumously behead Wilzig. While this shows her optimism, it may also hint at Lucy instinctively suppressing her true emotions or her method of coping. She also refuses to use harsh profanity as well at first, at least until after her first kill. [[File:FOTV Lucy attacks a woman.gif|thumb|250px|left|Lucy attacks a Vault 4 dweller by slamming her head into a pod]] Lucy has lived a privileged life without needing to deal with the roughness of the wasteland. She is also said to be naive due to her upbringing, as her only experience with the outside world has been through what she learned in the Vault and read in books.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240307175615/https://www.moviefone.com/news/10-things-we-learned-at-the-fallout-press-conference/ Moviefone: 10 Things We Learned at the ‘Fallout’ Press Conference with Cast and Crew (archived)] This is one of Lucy's dangerous flaws, and nearly leads to her and Maximus being killed when they encounter a pair of [[cannibalism|cannibals]] at a railroad bridge, even injuring Maximus. Lucy learns that she needs to exhibit a healthy degree of caution around strangers, and why she can not always trust human beings to do the right thing. It is also shown Lucy is not immune to peer pressure, seen when she unzips her jacket a little when the Vault 4 dwellers undress entirely. Lucy is confident that she can improve things, fueled by her optimism of the retro-America she was raised to admire. An optimistic, hard-working person, she has an inherent belief that humanity is generally good and that there is goodness in the world that can prevail over evil. However, she struggles to maintain this belief the more she explores the wasteland, becoming more cynical as she becomes aware of suffering, violence and death.[https://web.archive.org/web/20240404013830/https://www.fandom.com/articles/fallout-series-preview Fandom: Prime’s ‘Fallout’ Series Explores the Satirical Side of the End of the World (archived)] Her personality goes through a transformation when she finds herself betrayed and attacked by humanity, making her tougher and wiser, even if she becomes emotionally overwhelmed sometimes. [[File:FOTV Lucy weeps.png|thumb|250px|Lucy weeps after learning she can not trust her father]] Her breaking point takes place when she learns the truth about her father from Lee Moldaver, namely his involvement with Vault-Tec and in the destruction of Shady Sands, which killed thousands of innocent people. This only is worsened after realizing her mother was transformed into a ghoul in the process. Her entire world shatters, leaving her disgusted by her father and unable to see him as the same person she loved and wanted to rescue. She knows she can not rely on her father or Vault-Tec any longer. Nevertheless, Lucy still retains her kindness and cares for those who are close to her, being worried for Maximus when Hank knocks him out, going as far as grabbing Maximus' gun to hold her dad at gunpoint. She later doubts leaving Maximus to go with the Ghoul, however at the last moment she chooses to follow him to catch her dad and meet the people of Vault-Tec and before leaving, she ultimately kills her mother out of mercy and compassion. This contrasts her upset attitude when she saw the Ghoul kill Roger under similar circumstances, as Lucy now understands he did it to spare Roger from a fate like that of her mother. While she initially refuses to use violence, Lucy's time in the wasteland makes her more open to attacking and harming others. However, she still refuses to kill in cold blood, which is seen during her interaction with the [[Great Khans]], politely asking for a solution that doesn't involve violence and murder, but resorting to inflicting non-fatal injuries when negotiations fail. She explains to the Ghoul that she wants to set the example in doing things in a different way in the wasteland, wanting to arrest her father and bring him to justice rather than kill him for revenge like the Ghoul prefers to do. Furthermore, Lucy still tries to talk things through first, as seen when tries to negotiate with the Khans and when she approaches [[Old Woman Gretch]] peacefully, in contrast to the Ghoul, who's willing to pull a gun on her. Lucy's time outside of the vault has slowly made her more tolerant of the outside world's cruelty, being able to at least endure being near blood or dismembered bodies, remaining calm when the head of a man victimized by her father explodes, which only fuels her desire to make her father face justice. However, after being rescued from Caesar's Legion and becoming addicted to Buffout, Lucy becomes quicker and more eager to resort to underhanded tactics to achieve her goals, such as stealing not only the Addictol she needs, but also a power fist, not even trying to barter with the shopkeeper or at least talk through the meaning of the high price. She also becomes more unrestrained and willing to kill, picking a fight with and killing some feral ghoul Kings standing in her way, and later killing a thief who killed and is impersonating a shopkeeper in Freeside, though the latter was an accident and leaves her shocked at her own brutality. She also becomes mocking and dismissive of the NCR, referring to the two holdout members as nothing more than "matching jackets" behind their backs, despite seeking to bring Hank to justice for destroying the NCR capital, having lived there with mother and being aware of what they stood for, and having been shown unconditional kindness by them. This dismissiveness mirrors the Ghoul's disdain for Lucy, who treated her as nothing but a joke for her ideals while she tried to stand tall against it. After the incident in the shop, withdrawing from Buffout and being betrayed by the Ghoul, Lucy appears to have returned to her more compassionate self, bringing Hank MacLean to justice and insisting on shutting down the mainframe for the mind control devices to stop them from controlling people and being manufactured, even though they could be used against the Legion and she'd been attacked by one of the mind control subjects. Lucy wants to make the wasteland better, but does not want to do so through a "Peace of the Graveyard," as her father intends to do so with acts such as destroying Shady Sands or taking away people's free will. Despite previously demeaning them as "matching jackets," she believes that despite its issues, the NCR is not nearly as bad as the Legion, claiming that while the Legion tortures, kills and enslaves people, the NCR is "vaguely problematic."
